wa_sector_europa.blurb: Sector Europa is a small sport crag in the Metaline Falls climbing area of Washington's far northeast corner, at about 2,400 feet. Its eleven bolted lines run from an easy 5.6 up to the 5.13 range, but the bulk of them sit in the 5.12s, so it suits strong climbers best. The limestone here is overhanging and tufa-streaked in places, with a couple of longer, gentler slab pitches and some balancy vertical climbing for variety. The way down to the base involves a short ladder-style descent on rebar rungs, which gives the place a distinctly European feel.

wa_star_wars_boulders.blurb: The Star Wars boulders are a compact bouldering spot on Mountain Home Road, on the east side of Leavenworth in Washington's Central-East Cascades, at roughly 2,100 feet. It is among the best-known pockets of the boulder-scattered hillside, and many problems carry movie-themed names. Expect eleven problems with a wide spread: a few easy ones in the V1 to V3 range, then a steady climb into hard territory, with several problems at V9 and up. Landings are flat and the rock is steep, so this is a good stop for climbers who are chasing difficult, powerful lines.

wa_toats_coulee_middle_fork_loomis.blurb: A small, quiet cliff of about 150 feet high, sitting near 5,250 feet along the Middle Fork of Toats Coulee Creek at the southeast edge of the Pasayten Wilderness, west of Loomis. Climbing faces mostly south and southwest. Easier, broken ledges lie toward the right end of the south side, while the steeper, blank southwest face holds the harder lines. Eleven routes, mostly sport with a pair of trad lines, span roughly 5.7 to 5.12, with the majority at 5.7 to 5.10. Because the cliff is lightly travelled, loose rock is possible, so wear a helmet. A creekside campground sits close by, and Windy Peak fills the view to the north.

wa_b_lookout_wall.blurb: Lookout Wall is a little cliff in the summit group on Mount Erie, on Fidalgo Island, tucked below and to the left of Summit Wall. It has a vertical face with a couple of bolted lines, plus a dirty crack that takes a few trad routes. All told there are eleven climbs, mostly sport, with most of the grades clustered around 5.9 to 5.10 and a single 5.11 at the top end, along with a lone easy trad line. The wall sits directly beneath Lookout Point, and objects have been dropped from above, so a helmet is wise and the base is worth checking for glass.

wa_naughty_corner_boulders.blurb: Naughty Corner is a cluster of boulders in the Miller River zone of the Skykomish Valley, in the Central-West Cascades, at about 1,600 feet. The whole cluster formed when one giant block broke apart near the river, leaving a big slab on the river side and a set of aretes inside the broken pile. Eleven problems cover a broad range, from VB-level warm-ups through the mid grades to a few hard problems around V7 and V8. Low, easy problems sit close to the start of the trail, while the harder ones lie deeper inside the fractured block.

wa_420.blurb: The 420 is the most-visited cluster of the 420 Boulders in Icicle Creek canyon, outside Leavenworth, probably because it is the nearest to the road and only a short walk of about five minutes. It is a modest boulder with eleven problems, mostly in the V1 to V5 range with one harder problem near V7. It catches a good amount of direct sun, which makes it a handy option on cold days, and landings are flat. There are not many problems, but the standout one is worth the short walk.

wa_a_relief_camp.blurb: Relief Camp is the leftmost section of the Overhaul Area on the Far Side of Exit 38, near North Bend, at about 1,900 feet. It is a tall, steep, heavily featured wall, with overhanging ground and a cave on the left side. Holds are large and plentiful, so most of the eleven sport routes are sustained pulling on big handles, mostly 5.10 to 5.11 with a couple at 5.12 and one easier line near 5.8. A few ramps lead to the gentler climbs. Be aware the rock is loose in places, and a field of trundled debris sits at the base.
